originalTitle: Australia news live: Minns considers banning ebikes for under-12s in NSW; air safety chief says Sydney tarmac near-miss ‘unacceptable’
content: Police say the remains found in a suitcase near Goulburn are not human. Supt Linda Bradbury with NSW police said: Some good news here that we don’t have a suspicious death of a human on our hands. … We are still undertaking more forensic work to identify what they are. But we can identify that they’re not human. She said the idea is to not disturb crime scenes when they are discovered, which is why it took some time to determine the remains were not human. Bradbury did describe them as “very realistic in the terms of looking like human remains”. But we’ve confirmed by other means that they are not. Mortgage applications fall 20% at Westpac since budget Westpac has delivered a $1.8bn quarterly net profit even after mortgage applications fell due to a combination of higher interest rates and Labor’s property tax changes. The bank said in an update this morning that mortgage applications were down 20% between mid-May and the end of July, representing the immediate period after Labor announced changes to negative gearing and the treatment of capital gains. The tax changes have largely dented demand from investors, to the benefit of owner-occupiers. Mortgage applications were already falling ahead of the May budget due to the Reserve Bank’s string of interest rate hikes, designed to subdue inflation. Anthony Miller, Westpac’s chief executive, said ongoing housing undersupply would support prices. The undersupply of housing combined with population growth is expected to partially offset the impact of higher interest rates and recent federal government policy changes on the housing market. Overall, the bank recorded a 2% lift in lending during the June quarter, helping it increase its net profit result. The NSW premier, Chris Minns, says the government is examining introducing a minimum age of 12 to ride ebikes in the state, the strongest indication yet of where the government will land following an independent expert review. Minns appeared this morning to cut a gold ribbon on the debut of Kyle Sandilands Live, the new digital radio show hosted by the former Kiis FM host after the cancellation of the Kyle and Jackie O Show in March. The premier told Sandilands “I was worried for you” following the show’s cancellation, while the pair joked about running into each other recently at an ice-cream shop in the Blue Mountains. Sandilands said: I thought you were a meth head because you had had the beanie on, you were you all rugged up. But the conversation did turn towards policy, after Sandilands said he had bought his 11-year-old godson an ebike. The premier said the government is “examining an … age limit of 12” for ebikes. “We haven’t finalised the details yet,” he said. After a surge in injuries and an incident in which 40 or so e-bikes swarmed the Sydney Harbour Bridge in February, an expert review was asked to recommend an age limit of between 12 and 16, and was due to report back to the government in June. Safety bureau chief says near-miss at Sydney airport ‘unacceptable’ Angus Mitchell, the chief commissioner at the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB), told ABC Radio Sydney this morning the near-miss at Sydney airport was “a serious incident” that warranted investigation. Mitchell said while the two aircraft were moving at very low speeds, “separation of aircraft, whether it be in the air or on the ground is of vital importance, and there are systems in place to ensure that they are always separated”. “So what happened yesterday morning … it is unacceptable,” Mitchell said. So planes should not be getting that close and we should never have to rely on, as has happened in both these instances, pilots at the last minute, making an emergency decision to prevent them coming together. ATSB, Mitchell said, is gathering information about what happened surrounding the incident. He added that could include looking at the complexity of a new airport opening in western Sydney and new airspace design in that area. We have a lot of controllers that have come in very recently that are gaining their qualifications. So, look, I certainly don’t want to say that that’s what sits behind these two incidents because we don’t have all the facts. But we do know that that is a system that has had some significant challenges, as have airlines as well. The NSW government is rolling out a new scheme of smart rental bonds, which will allow some renters to transfer their bonds from one rental to the next when they move house. The scheme will end the need to save up thousands of dollars for a new bond before the old one is returned, and will begin with a phased rollout for renters in Parramatta, the Central Coast or Penrith local government areas. The scheme will ultimately be rolled out across the state by the end of the year. Renters will be notified when a new landlord or agent lodges a bond request online. They can then choose to pay their new bond upfront or use a smart rental bond to move it to the new rental for a $25 fee. Any difference in bond is either paid by the renter, or refunded if it is cheaper and there is no agreed claim on the bond. If the landlord at an original property makes a claim, the NSW government will pay the landlord directly and the renter will then pay the government. The premier, Chris Minns, said in a statement: Over two million people in New South Wales are renters – one of the highest proportions of the population ever living in rental accommodation. For a lot of renters, moving home can mean finding another $3,000 or $4,000 before you’ve even had your old bond returned. That’s a huge financial hurdle for families already doing it tough. Smart Rental Bonds removes that barrier by letting renters transfer their bond instead of paying for two at once. chineseContent: 警方表示，在古尔本附近的一个手提箱中发现的遗骸不是人类。新南威尔士州警方警长琳达·布拉德伯里 (Linda Bradbury) 表示：“这里有一些好消息，我们手上没有发现任何可疑的死亡事件。” ......我们仍在进行更多的法医工作来确定它们是什么。但我们可以确定他们不是人类。她说，这样做的目的是在发现犯罪现场时不要打扰它们，这就是为什么需要一些时间才能确定遗骸不是人类的原因。布拉德伯里确实将它们描述为“就看起来像人类遗骸而言非常逼真”。但我们通过其他方式证实事实并非如此。西太平洋银行 (Westpac) 的抵押贷款申请量下降了 20%，因为尽管利率上升和工党的财产税改革导致抵押贷款申请量下降，但西太平洋银行 (Westpac) 仍实现了 18 亿美元的季度净利润。该银行在今天上午的更新中表示，5 月中旬至 7 月底期间抵押贷款申请量下降了 20%，这是工党宣布改变负扣税和资本利得待遇后的一段时间。税收变化在很大程度上削弱了投资者的需求，从而使自住业主受益。由于央行为抑制通胀而进行的一系列加息，抵押贷款申请量已经在 5 月份预算之前出现下降。西太平洋银行首席执行官安东尼·米勒表示，持续的住房供应不足将支撑价格。住房供应不足加上人口增长预计将部分抵消利率上升和近期联邦政府政策变化对住房市场的影响。总体而言，该银行在六月份季度的贷款增长了 2%，帮助其提高了净利润。新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯 (Chris Minns) 表示，政府正在考虑引入
